title_en: Chinese Humor (10/20): Grilled at the New Year Table
note_en: 又…又… links two qualities or actions that are true at the same time, like English "both... and...": 小文又尴尬又无奈 "Xiao Wen felt both embarrassed and helpless." The two parts are usually the same kind of word (two adjectives or two verbs) and point the same way emotionally, reinforcing each other. Compare the set phrase 又爱又怕 at the end, "loved and dreaded at once," where the two feelings pull against each other for humorous effect.

sentences.en: These are the famous "Big Three New Year Questions" that circulate on the Chinese internet: "How much do you earn?", "Are you seeing anyone?", and "When are you getting married?" The older generation is used to showing concern this way, but young people feel they're being interrogated, which makes it a classic, unavoidable joke at the Spring Festival dinner table.
